name: Electrical Assisted Bicycle
description: A vehicle with two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 throttle to 20 mph, and Class 3 pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 and Class 3 assist only while the rider pedals, cutting out at 20 and 28 mph; Class 2 may assist without pedaling, to 20 mph
Class 1 and 3 need a cutoff that can't be bypassed, stopping the motor when the rider stops pedaling; a Class 2 motor stops when the brakes are applied
A vehicle modified out of every class, or built to be easily switched out of one by a button, setting or app, is not an electrical assisted bicycle
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-1-102(28.5), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: One whose motor exceeds 750 W, or that is modified out of its class, is a low-power scooter while its motor is 4,476 W or less with no manual clutch, needing a driver's license, registration and insurance, and a motorcycle past that, needing a motorcycle endorsement; one built for off-road use is an off-highway vehicle
A multiple-mode e-bike that can switch between classes must meet the rules of each class it can run as
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: A multiple-mode e-bike's label must name each class it can run as
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Carries a permanent label, in Arial at least 9-point, stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage, and must not be modified to change its speed or motor engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Breaking the equipment, label or modification rules is a class B traffic infraction
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221(11), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Sellers must tell the buyer its motor wattage, top speed and class, and for one that can run as Class 3, that riding a Class 3 under 16 is unlawful in Colorado
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221(13), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: A vehicle that isn't an e-bike can't be sold, in a store or online, labeled as a Class 1, 2, 3 or multiple-mode e-bike or represented as one
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221(12), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Advertising or selling a vehicle that isn't an e-bike with the words e-bike, electric bike or similar takes a written disclosure, in the store and on its website and social media marketing, that it isn't an e-bike under state law but a motor vehicle subject to motor vehicle laws on public roads and lands, which insurance may not cover
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221(12), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Selling a vehicle labeled or represented as an e-bike that isn't one, or without that disclosure, is a deceptive trade practice under the Colorado Consumer Protection Act
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §§42-4-221(12)(c), 6-1-105(1)(llll), as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Its lithium-ion battery must be certified by an accredited lab to a UL 2849 or EN 15194 battery standard
restrictions.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes §42-4-221, as amended by HB 25-1197

restrictions.rule: Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Class 3 riders must be 16 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Class 3 riders and passengers under 18 must wear a bicycle helmet meeting CPSC or ASTM standards, and a Class 3 must have a speedometer
Class 1 and Class 2 may ride bike and pedestrian paths where bicycles are allowed, but a local authority may ban them from its paths
Class 3 is kept off bike and pedestrian paths unless the path is within a street or highway or the local authority allows it
On a sidewalk it yields to pedestrians, and local ordinances or signs may ban it there
In state parks, Class 1 and 2 may ride roads, bike lanes and trails open to bicycles
In state wildlife areas, e-bikes are limited to roads and camping or parking areas open to motor vehicles
Its rider has the same rights and duties as a bicyclist, and it is not a motor vehicle: no registration or driver's license
